name: Eye Contact Consistency
algorithm: Eye Contact Consistency — Pixel-Level Spatial Analysis
mechanism:
This method analyzes eye contact patterns for deepfake detection:

1. **Gaze Direction Estimation**: Per-frame gaze direction is estimated from iris position, eye corner landmarks, and head pose. The gaze vector is decomposed into horizontal and vertical components relative to the camera, determining whether the subject appears to be making eye contact.

2. **Eye Contact Pattern Analysis**: Natural eye contact follows specific behavioral patterns — during conversation, humans alternate between direct eye contact and glancing away (typically maintaining eye contact 60-70% of time). The method models these patterns and checks whether the subject's gaze behavior follows expected psychological norms.

3. **Gaze-Head Coordination**: When shifting gaze, natural eye movements combine eye rotation (saccades) with head rotation in coordinated vestibulo-ocular patterns. The method verifies gaze-head coordination — deepfakes may produce eye movements decoupled from head motion or show unnaturally stable gaze during head turns.

4. **Bilateral Gaze Consistency**: Both eyes should converge on the same target point (vergence). The method checks that left and right eye gaze vectors intersect at a plausible depth. Deepfakes may produce strabismus-like artifacts where eyes appear to look in slightly different directions.

5. **Temporal Gaze Naturalness**: Gaze changes include saccades (fast, ballistic movements), smooth pursuit (tracking moving objects), and fixations (stable gaze). The method analyzes the temporal structure of gaze signals for correct velocity profiles. AI-generated eye movements often lack natural saccadic dynamics, producing either unrealistically smooth or jittery gaze patterns.
parameters:
Analysis type: pixel
Media: video
Input: Video frames extracted at key intervals
Output: Confidence score (0-100)
Frame sampling: Adaptive (1-5 fps depending on method)
Temporal window: Sliding window across frame sequence
accuracy: Moderate to High — 70-88% standalone accuracy. Most effective when combined with other video forensic methods. Performance depends on video quality, resolution, and compression level.
source: Video forensics and deepfake detection research. Based on computer vision and temporal signal analysis methods.
useCase: Detection of deepfake and AI-generated video through eye contact consistency analysis. This method examines temporal and spatial features that are difficult for AI systems to perfectly replicate, providing evidence for video authenticity assessment.
strengths:
• Captures temporal artifacts that single-frame analysis misses
• Works with standard video formats
• Effective against common deepfake techniques
• Can be combined with other video forensic methods
• Based on established computer vision research
limitations:
• Performance affected by video compression and resolution
• Some methods require sufficient frame count for temporal analysis
• Effectiveness varies with deepfake generation technique
• Best used as part of a comprehensive multi-method pipeline
• May produce false positives on heavily edited authentic video
